items.title: Noah Cook Interview, 1960-08-30
items.q: He was the head jockey at the fire ground. And he used to teach us how to ride... this boy used to train us.

ctx.x: They used to have a lot of them. A lot of them, yeah.

Plenty of them. There was three rides with me. The white boy, Roland Brown, his name was. He was the head jockey at the fire ground. And he used to teach us how to ride. You see, you've got to learn that. You can't get on a horse and say you're going to ride. And this boy used to train us. And I liked him four months of having, he had enough time to get a license. You can't ride in a race without license. And I just liked him four months. And that's why I left and went to the service. They had one out there in…
Did they have more color than white or more white than the car?
